anomalies.observed: On the USB page, the P-channel MOSFET Q1 (Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source pin 2 tied to +5V and its drain pin 3 tied to USB_C_VBUS_IN, while the LTC4412 U6 has pin 1 (IN) tied to USB_C_VBUS_IN and pin 6 (SENSE) tied to +5V.
anomalies.expected: For the LTC4412 ideal-diode USB power path, the P-channel MOSFET source should connect to the input side (USB_C_VBUS_IN / U6 IN) and the drain to the output side (+5V / U6 SENSE) so the body diode conducts input-to-output and reverse current is blocked.

evidence.quote: USB page: Q1 Q_PMOS_GSD pin 2 to +5V, pin 3 to USB_C_VBUS_IN; U6 LTC4412xS6 pin 1 to USB_C_VBUS_IN, pin 6 to +5V.
USB diode doesn't work, I guess need ideal diode to handle more power? LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly

anomalies.impact: The USB-C power path is oriented backwards; the MOSFET body diode can conduct from the board +5V rail into USB_C_VBUS_IN, defeating the intended reverse-current protection and possibly back-powering the USB port or preventing the ideal-diode controller from operating correctly.

parsed.summary: The drawing appears to contain a USB power-path error: the LTC4412-controlled P-channel MOSFET is source/drain swapped relative to the controller's IN/SENSE connections, so the intended reverse-current protection is not implemented.
